products.name: Goblin Tools
products.note: Found in the research for The AI Ready School; not independently verified. AI: AI task breakdown. Use: Task breakdown and tone tools. Who: Students, adults. Student age: Web version needs no account. Privacy: Not verified; no school agreement. Price: Web free; mobile app $2.99 one-time (App Store). Caution: Designed for neurodivergent users; consumer tool.

reading.body:
Goblin Tools is a free web utility with a $2.99 one-time mobile app, aimed at students and adults, and designed for neurodivergent users.

The pattern here is a small independent developer shipping a narrow AI function, task breakdown, with no account required on the web and no school agreement in place. The product is classified as education and research AI, but its stated audience is broader than schools. The mobile app is a one-time purchase rather than a subscription, which is unusual for AI tools and suggests the model runs cheaply or the developer is not recovering inference costs through recurring revenue.

For AI specifically, this is the low end of the compute curve. Task breakdown and tone adjustment are small, bounded operations that do not require frontier models or large training runs. Nothing in the data describes where the tool runs, what hardware it uses, or how much power it draws, so it cannot be used to say anything about data center demand. What it does show is that some AI products reach users without a school contract, a privacy review, or a recurring fee.

The data does not cover usage numbers, revenue, or whether the tool is still maintained. Privacy is listed as not verified, and the product note itself says it was found in research and not independently verified. The account feature is described only as the site describes it. A reader should treat this as a catalog entry, not an assessment.

profile_text.body:
Goblin Tools is an independent developer operating the website goblin.tools. According to its site, the tool has accounts that let users keep their history, sync lists across devices, and share them with anyone.

The product tracked is Goblin Tools, listed under Education and Research AI. It is described as an AI task breakdown tool, with task breakdown and tone tools, aimed at students and adults. The web version needs no account, and the mobile app is priced at $2.99 one-time on the App Store. The web version is free. It is noted as designed for neurodivergent users and as a consumer tool. Privacy terms have not been verified and there is no school agreement.

No lawsuits, MCP servers, or other filings are recorded for this company.
